Definition: from G575 and G3724; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.:--divide, separate, sever.
BiblicalUsage: To set apart, to separate — Paul separated unto the gospel of God, the Spirit saying separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work, God separating Paul from his mother's womb, and the call to come out from among them and be separate. The word draws a boundary, and the boundary is for a purpose.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe separation is not rejection but appointment: God sets his people apart so he can send them. And I hold that being set apart for the gospel is the highest calling there is.
